name: Form Configuration Best Practices
summary: Guidelines and best practices for generating high-quality JSON Forms configuration

layoutSelection.description: Choose the right root layout based on form complexity. The Design System's basic layout pattern uses the page stepper (Categorization with variant='pages') as the preferred method for complex government forms.

rules.condition: SIMPLE — none of the COMPLEX signals (a one-page document of a handful of fields stays simple even if a file was attached)
rules.recommendation: Use VerticalLayout as root. Do not promote it to Categorization.

rules.condition: COMPLEX — any of: ≥2 named sections; ≥1 conditional branch; ≥12 inputs; extracted text ≥8,000 characters or PDF ≥4 pages; existing definition already has ≥2 categories or ≥12 properties. When unsure, treat as complex.
rules.recommendation: Use Categorization with variant="pages" — the Design System's preferred basic layout pattern. This creates a Task List with section groupings, progress tracking, and a summary review page. Only COMPLEX generation may introduce Categorization.

rules.condition: The user explicitly asked for a stepper (not merely a multi-section form)
rules.recommendation: Use Categorization with variant="stepper" for a simple step navigation bar. Do not choose stepper just because the form is complex.

rules.condition: Exception — single-purpose contact/feedback with follow-up fields and no named Category headings
rules.recommendation: Stay on VerticalLayout. Use the Contact/Feedback Form with Conditional Routing example. Do not add Categorization just because one field has a SHOW rule.

documentUseCases.description: When a PDF or DOCX describes the form, classify the document's use case first, then reuse the matching examples. Do not force every document into the survey pattern or into Categorization.

conventions.meaning: Named section. Do not include the text "Category:" in the displayed Category label. Two or more named sections → COMPLEX pages.

Conditional SHOW group. Place a Group (or VerticalLayout fallback) with a SHOW rule as the last child of the category. Use enum in the rule condition when several trigger values apply. Pair SHOW + required with if/then (conditional-required example).
HelpContent with markdown true, using the exact wording from the document.
One field. Map Control to the matching UI Control example. Use exact option wording as enum values.
Radio Buttons (2–4 options, or a Likert/rating series that reuses the same enum).
String Control. If required, use the minLength: 1 workaround.
Multi-Select Checkboxes (array + uniqueItems + format checkbox). Set maxItems when Maximum selections is specified.
Omit from the required array. Unless the document says otherwise, questions are required.

conventions.signal: Name / address / email / phone / SIN / dependents
conventions.meaning: Prefer ADSP common schema $ref (personFullName, postalAddressAlberta, email, phoneNumber, socialInsuranceNumber, personDependents) instead of building from scratch.

formTypes.name: Contact, feedback, or complaint
documentSignals: follow-up fields that depend on category
formTypes.layout: SIMPLE VerticalLayout unless the document names 2+ categories or has 12+ inputs

formTypes.name: Eligibility calculator or computed totals
documentSignals: fees, grants, or amounts calculated from other answers
formTypes.layout: Follow SIMPLE vs COMPLEX from sections/inputs, then add computed fields

formTypes.name: Simple single-purpose intake
useExamples: Dropdown Select or Radio Buttons as specified

formTypes.name: Household, dependents, or other repeating people
documentSignals: list of children, dependents, employees, or previous addresses
formTypes.layout: Follow SIMPLE vs COMPLEX from the rest of the document
useExamples: Object Array (Simple Repeating Items) when each item has only 1–2 fields

formTypes.name: Shared lookup lists (ministries, provinces, programs)
documentSignals: ministry/program lists that change independently of the form
formTypes.layout: Does not change layout; wire a data register on the Control
useExamples: Data Register — Object Array with Label/Value Mapping

checks: All UI schema scopes reference properties that exist in the data schema
Required fields in data schema are clearly marked in the `required` array
Each Control has a valid scope starting with `#/properties/`
No orphaned required fields (every required field has a matching property)
Data schema `type` is `"object"` at the root level

rules: Include descriptive labels — property names are auto-converted to labels but may need refinement
Add inline help for complex fields using `options.help`
Use HelpContent elements for important notices, privacy statements, or instructions
Provide clear error messages in validation rules
Keep help text at grade 9 reading level for citizen-facing forms

commonFields.description: Use ADSP common schema definitions instead of building fields from scratch

fields.name: Full Name
fields.renders: First name, middle name, and last name input fields

fields.name: Address
fields.renders: Structured postal address (addressLine1, municipality, subdivisionCode, postalCode)

commonFields.usage: Use schemaDefinitionTool to load definitions, then reference them with $ref in data schema properties

iterativeWorkflow.description: How to build forms iteratively with the user
steps: Call formSchemaIndex at session start. Do not call formConfigurationRetrievalTool during generation
To build a form from a description or a requirements document, call formGenerationRun once and let it finish
formGenerationRun plans the pages and branches, then builds and saves each one, so never hand-build a multi-page form
Use formSchemaPatch only for a targeted change to content that already exists
Never send a multi-category schema to formConfigurationUpdateTool
Don't dump JSON — progress appears in the editor as the run saves each page
